source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. After the Mauryas
points: The fall of the Mauryas (c. 185 BCE) was followed by an 'age of reorganisation' — many **regional powers** rose across India.
In the north: the **Shungas** (founded by Pushyamitra Shunga).
Foreign rulers entered the north-west: **Indo-Greeks** (e.g. **Menander/Milinda**), **Shakas**, **Parthians** and the **Kushanas**.

sections.heading: 2. The Kushanas and Kanishka
points: The **Kushanas** ruled from Central Asia to north India; their greatest king was **Kanishka** (c. 1st–2nd century CE).
Kanishka **patronised Buddhism** (a Buddhist council); Buddhism spread along the **Silk Route** to Central Asia and China.
Two great schools of art flourished: **Gandhara** (Greek-influenced) and **Mathura** (indigenous) — the first images of the **Buddha** in human form.
The Kushanas issued fine **gold coins**.

sections.heading: 3. The Satavahanas
points: The **Satavahanas** ruled the **Deccan** (c. 2nd century BCE–2nd century CE).
Greatest ruler: **Gautamiputra Satakarni**; the dynasty used **metronymics** (named after mothers, e.g. Gautami-puta).
They grew rich on **trade** and patronised **Buddhist** sites (e.g. **Amaravati**).

sections.heading: 4. The Far South — Sangam Age
points: The **Tamil region (Tamilakam)** was ruled by three dynasties: the **Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas** (the 'muvendar' = three crowned kings).
**Sangam literature** (early **Tamil** poetry) is our main source for this age — assemblies (sangams) of poets at **Madurai** (Pandya capital).
Flourishing **Roman trade**: pepper and spices exported; **Roman coins** found in the south (see the **Periplus of the Erythraean Sea**).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Post-Mauryan: Shungas (Pushyamitra); north-west foreigners: Indo-Greeks (Menander), Shakas, Kushanas.
Kanishka (Kushana) = Buddhism + Silk Route; Gandhara & Mathura schools of art (first Buddha images).
Satavahanas = Deccan; Gautamiputra Satakarni; metronymics; Amaravati.
Tamil south: Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas (muvendar); Sangam literature; Madurai.
Roman trade → Roman coins in south India; source = Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Kanishka** was a **Kushana** king who promoted **Buddhism** and the Silk Route trade.
**Gandhara** art = Greek/Hellenistic influence; **Mathura** art = indigenous — both gave early **Buddha images**.
The three Tamil dynasties (**Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas**) — Sangam literature is in **Tamil**.
**Satavahanas** ruled the **Deccan** and used **metronymics** (named after mothers).
